extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and general readers of Plato's Republic and political/philosophical theory
extracted.subtask_description: Close commentary on Books V–VI of Plato's Republic extracting the normative prescriptions and evaluative criteria Plato advances for the ideal state, the guardians, philosophers-as-rulers, breeding and family arrangements, education, and conduct in war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of rulers and women
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulers shall select the men and the women who will form the guardian class; after selection they shall dwell in common houses and have their meals in common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is an act of the legislator; the rulers choose partners and households to secure the polity's needs. The social arrangement is designed to produce unity and to prevent private interests; communal living and common meals reinforce common bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention of licentiousness by instituting holy marriage festivals
rubrics_metrics.description: Licentiousness must be prevented; holy marriage festivals will be instituted and their holiness will be in proportion to their usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ritualized, state-controlled marriage festivals (hymeneals) timed for population control; holiness (sacral framing) is used instrumentally to secure compliance. The rulers may deploy ceremonial authority to shape sexual conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineered mating and eugenic pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: The good must be paired with the good, and the bad with the bad; the rulers will contrive by an ingenious system of lots that the brave and the fair come together, and those of inferior breed with inferiors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers may use deception (make people ascribe pairings to chance) and even 'a strong dose of falsehood' to bring about desirable unions; offspring of the good are reared, others destroyed, to preserve the flock in prime condition. (Commentary notes practical and ethical problems with this scheme.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Communal child‑rearing and suppression of maternal recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: When children are born, offspring of the brave and fair will be carried to an enclosure and attended by suitable nurses; mothers will be brought to the fold to suckle but must not recognise their own offspring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hired nurses and attendants to transfer childcare burdens and prevent parental recognition; the arrangement is intended to create many parents for each child and erase private family ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age limits for procreation and penalties for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Parents ought to be in the prime of life: for a man reckoned at thirty years—from twenty-five to fifty-five; for a woman from twenty to forty. Anyone above or below those ages who partakes in the hymeneals is guilty of impiety; forming a marriage connection at other times without rulers' consent is forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state prescribes biologically‑framed age windows for legitimate procreation and treats violations as religious/constitutional offences; after the specified ages citizens may 'range at will' subject to incest prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and prohibition of certain affinities
rubrics_metrics.description: Degrees of affinity are regulated: brothers and sisters are those born seven or nine months after the espousals; parents are those espoused at the time—some degrees (parents/children) are prohibited, while brother/sister unions are not absolutely prohibited if a dispensation is procured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scheme attempts to abolish private kinship by redefining relations according to festival timing; commentary highlights ambiguities and practical impossibilities in this method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity as the highest good of the State
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest good of a State is unity; the greatest evil is discord and distraction. There will be unity where there are no private pleasures or pains or interests—where if one member suffers all the members suffer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institutional arrangements (common property, common family) are justified instrumentally by their tendency to produce solidarity and to make the State respond as a whole to harms and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common property to prevent disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens will have all things in common; with common property they will have common pleasures and pains—there will be no lawsuits about property when men have nothing but their bodies which they call their own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abolish private property among guardians to remove the causes of domestic strife, flattery of the rich, household cares, borrowing and not paying; commentary notes this intends to eliminate incentives to contention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military adaptation of communal arrangements and training
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle of communism is adapted to military service: parents will take their children to look on at a battle to train them, young warriors must learn under experienced veterans and be taught to ride.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military socialization uses public spectacles and apprenticeship-like observation (as potters’ boys by the wheel) to inculcate bravery; place youth under veterans and provide swift steeds—training emphasizes supervised exposure, not reckless endangerment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewards for bravery and sanctions for cowardice
rubrics_metrics.description: Cowards and deserters shall be degraded to the class of husbandmen; the hero shall be crowned, receive the right hand of fellowship, be kissed, have more wives and more to eat, and be honoured after death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honorific and material rewards (food, seating, wives, ritual crowns) mark social valuation; punishments degrade status and assign menial roles—honors are publicly conferred, backed by poetic authority (Homer) to reinforce courage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on wartime conduct and treatment of Hellenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Hellenes should not be enslaved; the dead should not be despoiled; Hellenic arms should not be offered up in temples; houses should not be burnt nor more than the annual produce carried off. War between Hellenes is civil war and should aim at reconciliation and punishment of guilty persons, not mass enslavement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate civil from foreign war; apply humane/limited conduct among kin-states and restrict plunder and devastation; emphasis on patriotic but restrained warfare and restoration of peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ritual and public opinion to secure compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ritual (holy festivals) and public explanations (making people ascribe arrangements to chance) will be used to secure compliance with legislated pairings and social rules; rulers may need to use falsehoods for desirable ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrumental use of stories/myths and manipulated lotteries to stabilize social engineering; the text candidly admits deliberate falsehoods as a tool of governance—commentary notes moral and practical objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophers as ideal rulers (qualities required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophers should be chosen as rulers if they have the other qualities required: lovers of the knowledge of the eternal and of all truth; haters of falsehood; meaner desires absorbed in interests of knowledge; spectators of all time and existence; free from fear of death; social, gracious, without cowardice or arrogance; learn and remember easily; harmonious, well-regulated minds; to whom truth flows by nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rulers' intellectual and moral profile is demanding—contemplate absolute ideas, subordinate personal appetites, possess practical social virtues; commentary stresses rarity of such characters and practical difficulties in finding them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and testing of guardians: gymnastic then dialectic
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should begin with gymnastics in youth and progress to 'gymnastics of the soul'; dialectic (the longer road) and the highest branches of knowledge must later be pursued; guardians must be tested in pleasures and pains and in intellectual virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reverse the usual order: bodily training first, then progressively rigorous intellectual training culminating in dialectic and knowledge of the idea of the good; guardians must undergo experiential tests (refiner's fire) to prove steadiness under pleasure and pain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrality of dialectic and ascent to the idea of the good
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialectic is the real difficulty to be mastered; the ascent proceeds from the visible (shadows, reflections, natural objects) through mathematics to the intelligible, finally resting in the idea of the good—the cause of knowledge and being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum must include mathematics as a stage and then reasoned dialectic using hypotheses to ascend to the good; the analogy of sun (good) and light (truth) structures education—failure to study dialectic leaves opinion, not knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between true philosophers and sophists/men of opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: True philosophers recognize abstract ideas (justice, beauty, good); false philosophers or sophists are lovers of opinion, of sights and sounds, flattery of the crowd, speaking of persons not principles; they are corrupting or merely echo public taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate philosophical character by orientation to universals vs flattery of popular opinion; beware of 'pretenders' who seek status or wealth or adapt to public taste rather than pursue truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability of philosophers to corruption and social pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophers are rare and are damaged by corrupting influences (public opinion, wealth, honours); the best natures may turn out the worst in unsuitable soil while weak natures seldom produce great good or evil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize social causes of moral failure: flattery (e.g., Alcibiades), exile, or death can destroy philosophers; the polity must either compel philosophers to hold office or have rulers' offspring love philosophy to realize the ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical critique: applicability and internal contradictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Plato's communistic proposals contain defects: no account of application to lower classes; the table of prohibited degrees is not practicable; new affinities may be arbitrary (based on month/year of birth); manipulation of lots is unexplained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any program of radical social engineering must be coherent and practicable—avoid arbitrary rules that cannot be implemented or that rest on accidental facts; the commentary flags logical/administrative shortcomings as anti-patterns.
